terms.definition: Elastic File System — a fully managed, elastic, POSIX-compliant NFS file system that multiple EC2 instances can mount and use simultaneously
terms.example: Like a shared network drive that every server in your office can read and write at the same time

terms.definition: A protocol that allows a computer to access files over a network as if they were on local disk; EFS uses NFSv4
terms.example: The same protocol used on Linux servers in on-premises data centers for decades

terms.definition: An NFS endpoint with an IP address and DNS name, created in a specific AZ subnet, through which EC2 instances connect to an EFS file system
terms.example: The front door to EFS in a particular Availability Zone — instances in that AZ connect through this door

terms.definition: Portable Operating System Interface — a standard for Unix/Linux file system behavior including permissions, ownership, and directory structure; EFS is POSIX-compliant
terms.example: Standard Linux chmod, chown, and file permission commands work on EFS files exactly as on local disk

terms.definition: The default EFS performance mode, optimized for the lowest latency per file operation — recommended for most workloads
terms.example: Best for web servers, CMS platforms, home directories — anything where individual file response time matters

terms.definition: An EFS performance mode optimized for highest aggregate throughput at the cost of slightly higher per-operation latency — designed for massively parallel workloads
terms.example: Best for big data analytics or genomics pipelines where 500 instances are reading simultaneously

terms.definition: The default EFS throughput mode where throughput scales automatically with workload demand — pay only for what you use
terms.example: Perfect for variable workloads — throughput rises when you need it and costs nothing during idle periods

terms.definition: An EFS throughput mode where you specify a fixed MiB/s regardless of file system size — for when you need more throughput than the size-based allocation provides
terms.example: A 10GB video editing file system that needs 500 MiB/s throughput — provisioned solves the mismatch

terms.definition: An EFS throughput mode where the file system earns burst credits during idle periods and spends them during high-activity bursts
terms.example: Like a phone battery — charges slowly when idle, depletes quickly when you're actively using it

terms.definition: The default multi-AZ EFS storage class for frequently accessed files — highest availability and durability
terms.example: Your production web application's shared media directory

terms.definition: Multi-AZ EFS storage class for infrequently accessed files — lower storage cost but a per-request retrieval fee applies
terms.example: Compliance documents accessed 2-3 times a year but stored for 7 years

terms.definition: Single-AZ EFS storage class — lower cost than Standard but no cross-AZ redundancy; data may be lost in AZ failure
terms.example: Dev/test environment files that can be recreated if lost

terms.definition: The lowest-cost EFS storage class — single AZ plus infrequent access pricing; highest risk, lowest cost
terms.example: Archive data in a dev account that hasn't been touched in 90+ days

terms.definition: An EFS feature that automatically moves files between Standard and IA storage classes based on how recently they were accessed
terms.example: Configure: move files not accessed in 30 days to Standard-IA — saves up to 92% on storage for cold files

terms.definition: An application-specific entry into an EFS file system that enforces a POSIX user identity and a root directory for all connections through it
terms.example: Microservice A connects via access point /app-a and can only see that directory; it has no access to /app-b

terms.definition: The NFS port used by EFS for all file system communication — must be allowed in security groups for EC2 instances to mount EFS
terms.example: Security group rule: inbound TCP port 2049 from the EC2 security group ID

terms.definition: An AWS-provided package for EC2 that simplifies EFS mounting, adds TLS encryption in transit support, and integrates with CloudWatch for monitoring
terms.example: Install with yum install -y amazon-efs-utils; mount with: sudo mount -t efs fs-xxxxxxxx:/ /mnt/efs

terms.definition: A Linux /etc/fstab option that instructs the OS to wait for network availability before mounting the EFS file system at boot
terms.example: Prevents EC2 from getting stuck at boot trying to mount EFS before the network interface is ready

terms.term: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
terms.definition: A fully managed Windows file system (SMB protocol) — the correct choice for shared storage on Windows EC2 instances; EFS only supports Linux
terms.example: When you hear Windows + shared storage in AWS → FSx for Windows, not EFS

terms.definition: Standard Unix/Linux file permission model (read/write/execute for owner, group, others) — fully supported by EFS
terms.example: chmod 644 /mnt/efs/config.txt works identically on EFS as it does on a local Linux disk
